Resolves #18642

🌿 A projection repair used to jump the queue it was meant to join, running beside the commit that had already taken its place; now a repair waits its turn and, finding a newer document scheduled, has nothing left to say.

`onDockProjectionFailed` scheduled its one clean re-projection by replacing `refreshPromise` with `timeout(0).then(retry)`, while every commit schedules off the settled tail. A commit that landed while the failing refresh was in flight was already chained on that refresh, so the repair ran beside it as soon as it suspended on a VDom-worker round-trip, and it re-projected the failed cycle's snapshot rather than the document of record. The repair now joins the tail exactly as a commit does and stands down when a newer document has been scheduled since — `projectDockZoneDocument` records the document it schedules as a `{document}` record in `scheduledProjection`, held by identity because the plain path assigns `dockModel` after the funnel returns and the Group path leaves it to the consumer's `setDocument`, and as a record because a scheduled `null` (the clear) must not read as nothing scheduled yet. With no newer commit the behaviour is unchanged: one repair, `isDockProjectionRetry`, no third attempt. The docblock that documented the replacement as the design is rewritten to the chain and the stand-down.

Evidence: L2 (unit tier: a real projecting host, the reconciler failing once and suspending on one macrotask, the App worker's shape) → L2 required. Residual: none — the App-worker overlap is the unit arm's modelled subject and has no flagship-only observable beyond it; the #18621 link is that ticket's.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — 1160 → 1164 code lines (on top of #18635's 1160): the `scheduledProjection` field and its one write at the projection funnel, plus two lines where the repair chains onto the tail instead of replacing it. The retry path this corrects already lives in this file and no consumer line became deletable, so the four lines are declared as growth rather than paid for.

## Deltas from ticket
The field the ticket proposed as `scheduledDocument` ships as `scheduledProjection`, a `{document}` record: a bare field that starts out `null` cannot tell a scheduled clear (`onDockZoneDocumentChange(null)`) from nothing scheduled yet, and the stand-down read the clear as the latter (R1, @neo-gpt-emmy). The record keeps the never-funnelled direct repair alive and stands the retry down behind a clear. The stand-down is a fire-time check inside the chained continuation and returns, so awaiters of `refreshPromise` settle.
